_source: Transcribed from the GWMS Curriculum Guide in Notion. Per-session fields come from that session's Lesson and Intervention Guide (Unit 7). Card, domain and keyCondition come from the GWMS Technical Map. Where the two name the game differently, the Lesson and Intervention Guide wins, because it is the per-session authority.

stage.name: The Return
stage.grapplingTlo: By the end of the Return, participants will apply and integrate back-pin control and finishing, holding total control without harm, and analyze the distance traveled since Session 1.
stage.caselTlo: By the end of the Return, participants will apply responsible decision-making to name what changed, contribute to others, set a standard for who comes next, and choose what to carry forward, analyzing the cost and worth of those choices.
stage.connection: Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program. Now you carry that choice out the door.

wrongAnswers.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
wrongAnswers.feedback: Never. You let go the second your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.

wrongAnswers.text: Hurting your partner because you can
wrongAnswers.feedback: That is the one thing the Back Pin teaches you never to do. Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program.

sessions.probingQuestion: What's actually different in you now?
sessions.keyCondition: Chest on their back, with hips, shoulders, and head wedge locked together. Hold for a three-count.
sessions.gameName: Back Take, Maintain Chest to Back Contact
sessions.gameText: Take the back and hold it. Keep your chest on their back for a three-count. Use light resistance.
sessions.gameNote: Twelve weeks ago, you could not hold this position. Now you can. That is change you can feel, not just talk about.
sessions.gameWin: Holding chest-on-back contact for a three-count against light resistance
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use back-pin control to take and hold the back, and name what they can do now that they could not do at the start.
grapplingElos: Take and hold the back-pin position for a three-count against light resistance.
Name one control skill they have now that they did not have in the Descent.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name what is really different in them now, and find real proof of the change instead of just talking about it.
caselElos: Name one real change in themselves since Session 1.
Tell apart a change they can show from one they only talk about.
sessions.connection: Twelve weeks ago, you could not hold this position at all. Now you can. That is proof of change you can feel. Naming what is different in you works the same way. Real change is something you can show, not just say.
sessions.takeaway: Change you can show is real change.

sessions.probingQuestion: How do you know the change is real and not just talk?
sessions.keyCondition: Hold the back while a live partner runs their 4S escape.
sessions.gameText: Hold the back while your partner tries hard to get out. Win by staying chest to back while they fight to turn in or get flat.
sessions.gameNote: A change that only works when things are easy is not real yet. This tests it under pressure.
sessions.gameWin: Staying chest to back while the partner fights to get flat or turn in
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use back-pin control while their partner fights back, and find out if the change holds up when tested.
grapplingElos: Keep the back for a three-count while the partner works hard to escape.
Notice whether their control holds under pressure or slips.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will test if a claimed change is real by checking it under pressure, and name the proof.
caselElos: Say how they would know a change is real.
Name one piece of proof that the change holds under stress.
sessions.connection: A change that only works when it is easy is not a real change yet. Holding the back against a fighting partner puts it to the test. Who you have become gets proven the same way, by whether it holds up when things get hard.
sessions.takeaway: Tested change is change you can trust.

sessions.probingQuestion: What can you do now that the old you couldn't?
sessions.keyCondition: Get the back from a fast, moving start.
sessions.gameName: Back to Chest Control Transition Game
sessions.gameText: Take the back during a live scramble. Reach a controlling position and stay on top.
sessions.gameNote: Name the exact thing you can do now that you could not before. Not just "better." The specific thing.
sessions.gameWin: Taking the back from a live scramble and reaching a controlling position while staying on top
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will get back-pin control from a live scramble, and name the exact skill they gained since the Descent.
grapplingElos: Get the back during a fast, live exchange.
Name a specific mat skill they own now that they did not before.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name one exact skill they have now that they did not have before.
caselElos: Name one clear new skill.
Connect it to a real situation where it matters.
sessions.connection: There is one exact thing you can do on the mat now that you could not before, and you can name it. Your growth off the mat works the same way. Not "I am better," but "I can do this now."
sessions.takeaway: You can name what you gained, exactly.

sessions.keyCondition: Keep control while you guide a newer partner. Do not just finish them.
sessions.gameName: Chest-to-Back Position Maintenance, run as a coaching round
sessions.gameText: Hold the back, but run it as a coaching round. Guide a newer partner through the position instead of just finishing them.
sessions.gameNote: You stop being the one getting helped and start being the help.
sessions.gameWin: Keeping control while guiding a newer partner through the position
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use back-pin control while helping a newer partner learn, and tell apart coaching from winning.
grapplingElos: Guide a newer partner through the back-pin position instead of only finishing them.
Notice the difference between coaching a partner and beating them.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will find who needs what they have learned, and turn the work outward.
caselElos: Name one person or group who could use what they have gained.
Name one thing they could offer them.
sessions.connection: Helping a newer partner instead of just tapping them out is the first act of giving on the mat. Turning your growth toward someone who needs it works the same way in life. You stop being the one who gets helped. You start being the help.
sessions.note: Not everyone is ready to give yet. That is okay. Nothing here is owed.
sessions.takeaway: You have something worth giving now.

sessions.probingQuestion: What can you give that actually costs you something?
sessions.keyCondition: Hold control, but give your partner room to work their escape.
sessions.gameName: Back Control Elbow Management, No Hooks
sessions.gameText: Hold the back with no hooks in. Manage the elbows, and give the bottom partner room to work their escape. Win by keeping control while you let them fight.
sessions.gameNote: Real giving costs you the easy finish.
sessions.gameWin: Keeping control while deliberately giving the partner room to work
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use back-pin control while letting a partner work and learn, and name what it costs to give that up.
grapplingElos: Hold back-pin control while deliberately giving the partner room to work.
Name what it costs to help instead of dominate.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name a contribution that costs them something real.
caselElos: Tell apart easy giving from giving that costs something.
Name one thing worth giving that costs them.
sessions.connection: Letting a partner work when you could just finish them costs you the easy win. Giving something real off the mat costs something too, time, comfort, pride. The giving that counts is the kind you feel.
sessions.note: Giving that costs you is not the same as erasing yourself. Giving until nothing is left of you is not the goal.
sessions.takeaway: The giving that costs is the giving that counts.

sessions.probingQuestion: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?
sessions.keyCondition: Full control, with your partner completely safe.
sessions.gameText: Take total control from the back. Turn the partner over while keeping them completely safe.
sessions.gameNote: You have their back. You hold all the power there is. And you choose not to hurt them. That is the whole point: strength used for someone, not over them.
sessions.gameWin: Turning the partner over from total back control while keeping them completely safe
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use full back-pin control without hurting the partner, and name the choice to control without harm.
grapplingElos: Keep total back control while keeping the partner completely safe.
Name the moment control could become harm, and the choice not to cross it.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name how they use their strength to help others, not to control them.
caselElos: Tell apart power that helps from power that controls.
Name one way to use their strength without putting someone else down.
sessions.connection: You can have full control of someone's back and still choose not to hurt them. That is the whole system: the power to hurt, and the choice not to. Using your strength for people instead of over them is that same choice, made in your life.
sessions.takeaway: Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, that is the whole point. You just held it in your hands.

sessions.probingQuestion: What do you want to leave behind you here?
sessions.keyCondition: The locking hand closes behind the head. The choking elbow sits on the chin line. Release it the instant they tap.
sessions.gameText: The back strangle is the sharpest finish in the system. Build the locking grip behind the head, elbow on the chin line. Release it the instant your partner taps.
sessions.gameNote: How you use the finish, controlled and clean, is what people remember about rolling with you. That is legacy.
sessions.gameWin: Building the locking grip behind the head, and releasing the instant your partner taps
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use the back strangle with control, and name what kind of training partner they have been.
grapplingElos: Get the back strangle against light resistance, and release on the tap.
Name what kind of partner they have been to the room.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name what they want to leave behind them.
caselElos: Name the mark they want to leave.
Connect it to how they act now.
sessions.connection: The finish is the sharpest power in the system. How you use it, controlled, releasing on the tap, is what people remember about rolling with you. What you leave behind in life is built the same way, out of how you treat people when you hold the power.
sessions.note: The jaw-based counters are not taught yet. They wait until the Therapeutic Manager approves them. Coaches do not teach them.
sessions.takeaway: Legacy is built from how you act now, not someday.

sessions.probingQuestion: What standard are you setting for whoever comes next?
sessions.keyCondition: Anchor the shoulder and control the wrist before you extend. Release on the tap.
sessions.gameName: Chest to Back to Precursor Transitions Game
sessions.gameText: The arm lock from the back. Move through the setup grips. Anchor the shoulder and control the wrist before you extend. Release on the tap.
sessions.gameNote: How you act here, controlled and clean, is the standard the next person copies.
sessions.gameWin: Moving through the setup grips with the shoulder anchored and the wrist controlled before any extension
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will use the arm lock from the back with control, and name how their actions set the standard for the room.
grapplingElos: Get the back arm lock with control, and release on the tap.
Name one way their actions set a standard others follow.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name the standard they set for whoever comes after them.
caselElos: Name the standard their behavior sets right now.
Name whether it is the one they want to set.
sessions.connection: How you carry yourself in the room, how you finish, how you treat a new partner, quietly sets the bar for everyone watching. The standard you set for whoever comes next in life works the same way. How you act is the standard.
sessions.takeaway: How you act is the standard, so choose it on purpose.

sessions.probingQuestion: If someone watched how you carry yourself, what would they learn?
sessions.keyCondition: Move between back control and your finishes. Always honor the tap.
sessions.gameText: Move between back control and your finishes during live rolling. Always honor the tap.
sessions.gameNote: Newer people learn more from watching you roll than from anything you say. This is the lesson you are teaching without a word.
sessions.gameWin: Moving between back control and your finishes with the tap honored
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will put back-pin control and finishing together in open rolling, and name what a watcher would learn from how they train.
grapplingElos: Move between back control and their finishes in live rolling, and release on the tap.
Name what a newer student would learn watching them roll.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name what someone would learn from watching how they carry themselves.
caselElos: Name the lesson their actions teach without words.
Decide if it is the lesson they want to teach.
sessions.connection: Newer people learn more from watching how you roll than from anything you say. How you carry yourself in life teaches the same way, silently, to whoever is watching. You are a lesson whether you mean to be or not.
sessions.note: This is about influence, not being watched and judged. Nobody is grading how you carry yourself.
sessions.takeaway: You are a lesson already, so be the one you would choose to teach.

sessions.probingQuestion: What did this cost you, and what did you get for it?
sessions.keyCondition: Play both roles, control on top and 4S escape underneath.
sessions.gameName: Back Control with Multiple Arm Escape Options (deliberate capstone-week exception, Intermediate tier)
sessions.gameText: Play both roles. On the back, control and finish. Underneath, work the arm escapes against a live grip.
sessions.gameNote: Twelve weeks of getting tapped and rebuilt, and now you can do both sides. That is the honest ledger.
sessions.gameWin: Playing both roles — controlling and finishing on top, working the escapes underneath
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will put the full back-pin game together in open rolling, and name what twelve weeks of training cost them and gave them.
grapplingElos: Roll open from the back-pin game, controlling and finishing with the tap honored.
Name what the training cost and what it gave.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name the honest cost and reward of the whole program.
caselElos: Name what the twelve weeks cost them.
Name what they got for it.
sessions.connection: Twelve weeks of getting tapped, cracked, and rebuilt cost something and gave something. Rolling now, you can feel both in your body. The honest ledger of what this cost and what you got is the first step of the return.
sessions.note: Grief and pride both belong here. Neither one cancels the other.
sessions.takeaway: The ledger is honest, and it landed on the side of growth.

sessions.keyCondition: Stay in control and stay calm during live rolling.
sessions.gameName: Chest to Back No Hooks Game (same capstone-week exception as 34)
sessions.gameText: The full back game, live, with no hooks handed to you. Stay in control and stay calm, start to finish.
sessions.gameNote: The person rolling now is not the one from Session 1, and you can see it.
sessions.gameWin: Rolling the full back game with control and calm, start to finish
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will show the full back-pin game as the person they have become, and name how far they have come since Session 1.
grapplingElos: Roll the back-pin game with control and calm.
Name how far they have come since Session 1.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name who they became over the program.
caselElos: Describe the person they are now.
Compare that to who walked in on Session 1.
sessions.connection: The person rolling now is not the one who walked in on Session 1. You can see the difference in how you move. Naming who you became is the return itself, not who you were told to be, but the one you built.
sessions.takeaway: You became someone, and you built them yourself.

sessions.probingQuestion: What do you carry out this door?
sessions.keyCondition: A final live roll, tap honored, then the walk out the door.
sessions.gameName: First to Chest-to-Back: Find, Maintain, and Submit (same capstone-week exception as 34 and 35)
sessions.gameText: The last roll of the program. Find the back. Hold it. Finish with the tap honored. Then you walk out the door.
sessions.gameNote: The mat was never the point. What you carry out of it is.
sessions.gameWin: Finding the back, maintaining it, and submitting with the tap honored
sessions.grapplingTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will show the whole back-pin game one last time, and name what from the training carries beyond the room.
grapplingElos: Complete a final live roll, controlling and finishing with the tap honored.
Name what of the mat carries into life.
sessions.caselTlo: By the end of this session, the participant will name what they carry out of the program into the rest of their life.
caselElos: Name what they take with them.
Commit to one way they will use it.
sessions.connection: The last roll ends, and then you walk out the door. What you carry out, control, mercy, the ability to stay, the real self, is the whole point. The mat was never the destination. What you carry out of it is.
sessions.takeaway: You descended and met yourself. You were initiated and tested against others. You returned, and you carry it out with you.
